To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) long HIV-1 LTR readthrough transcripts can be detected, 2) Egr-1 transcriptional activation is one of the cellular genes modified by HIV-1 infection, and 3) despite an increase of Egr mRNA, the amount or half-life of Egr- 1 protein does not seem to be modified in chronically infected T and promonocytic cells.

a chimeric transcript was found to consist of the 3’ end of the LRT of HIV-1 proviral sequence, followed by 3700 bp of cellular RNA, and that Egr-1 mRNAs were detected as an overrepresented transcript in HIV-1-infected promonocytic cells and T cell line.
HIV-1 infection induces the expression of the transcription factor EGR-1 in both T and monocytic cells and that EGR-1 is involved in HIV-2 replication in T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of cellular genes that are modified in HIV- 1 infected cells.
the identification and characterisation of cellular genes whose expression is modified by HIV-1 and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying this modification.
the identification of the pathways involved in the modification of cellular gene regulation during the course of HIV-1 infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIV-1 LTR can induce a long readthrough transcript and that this phenomenon could be one of the ways in which HIV-1 can modify cellular gene expression.
the increase of EGR-1 in HIV-1 infection does not appear to be a general phenomenon but rather an individual cellular response.
HIV-1 infection of U937 cells leads to a significant increase in Egr-1 transcription and a subsequent increase in the level mRNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-1 infection induces a modification of the cellular transcription profile in a cell type specific manner.
HIV-1 infection induces an increase of Egr1 expression, and that Egr-1 may be involved in the modification of cellular gene regulation by HIV-1.
HIV-1 infection of U937 cells induces the production of long HIV-1 LTR readthrough transcripts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
long readthrough transcripts may play a role in the modification of the cellular gene expression profile of chronically infected cells.
long readthrough transcripts are generated in HIV-1-infected cells and that Egr-1 is one of the genes over-expressed in HIV-1 infection.
HIV-1 can induce a specific increase of Egr1 mRNA in infected cells.
